# Clarified specification for `executable` The required artifact is a runnable command-line program named exactly `executable`. It is a single-purpose HTML-to-Markdown converter. All text input and output described below is UTF-8. ## Spec 1 The program has one conversion mode and no subcommands. Options are supplied directly to `executable`; bare positional arguments (including words such as `convert`, `help`, and `version`) are invalid. The supported interface is: ```text -v, --version --help --input PATH --output PATH --output-overwrite --domain URL --exclude-selector SELECTOR (repeatable) --include-selector SELECTOR (repeatable) --opt-strong-delimiter VALUE --plugin-strikethrough --plugin-table --opt-table-cell-padding-behavior VALUE --opt-table-header-promotion --opt-table-newline-behavior VALUE --opt-table-presentation-tables --opt-table-skip-empty-rows --opt-table-span-cell-behavior VALUE ``` For value options, both `--name value` and `--name=value` forms work. `--` ends option parsing; every token after it is consequently a positional argument and is rejected. Successful conversions and informational flags exit 0. Usage, validation, and I/O failures exit 1. Successful conversion writes no stderr; failures write no conversion data to stdout. There must be no ANSI color sequences. ## Spec 2 `--version` prints the following bytes to stdout and exits 0 with empty stderr. `-v` is the short form and has the same version-reporting behavior. ```text html2markdown GitVersion: dev GitCommit: none BuildDate: unknown ``` There is one newline after `unknown` and no leading newline. ## Spec 3 `--help` takes precedence even if a later option is invalid (for example, `--help --bogus` still succeeds), prints the following byte-exact text to stdout, and writes nothing to stderr. The output begins with one newline and ends with two newlines.
